chapter: The Second Herd and its sidemen
title: Billy Bauer: inhibited guitarist and small-group gems
summary: Bauer was inhibited and anxious, but full of ideas; he later studied with Tristano and appeared at the 40th anniversary.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah, he did. Can we talk a little bit about Billy Bauer? Because -- yeah.
Well, he was a very unusual guy, a very inhibited man.

Oh, yeah, very. And the only time he gave out was in his music. But everything else, he was very in himself and he had complexes and things. For awhile, while we were (inaudible) touring theatres, he said there was a guy following the band around, kept sitting in the balcony.

Who was trying to get his gig. And he kept saying, 'Man, you ain't making it. Now, you don't really play' you know. So we used to worry about Billy. But he was full of ideas and some of the earliest sounds we did, like, some of
the small group things, like "Four Men On A Horse," (inaudible).
Now, he left you and then went back to work and study with Lennie Leonard Tristano.
Yeah, that's right. And he's still playing. He's still around New York. And I run into him once in awhile. As a matter of fact, we had him at the 40th anniversary.
That's the first time -- he I used to be out with an ice the night show or something, traveling just -- getting into the wierdest things.
